facts: The study proposes a knowledge-independent method for aligning terms.
Translations are extracted from a small, domain-specific corpus.
The corpus consists of parallel English and Chinese court judgments from Hong Kong.
The study uses a sentence-aligned corpus.
Translation equivalences are suggested by analysing the frequency profiles of parallel concordances.
The method overcomes the limitations of conventional statistical methods.
Conventional statistical methods require large corpora to be effective.
The method overcomes the limitations of lexical approaches.
Lexical approaches depend on existing bilingual dictionaries.
Pilot testing was conducted on a parallel corpus of about 113K Chinese words and 120K English words.
Pilot testing gives an encouraging 85 % precision.
Future work includes fine-tuning the algorithm upon the analysis of the errors.
Future work includes acquiring a translation lexicon for legal terminology by filtering out general terms.
entities: parallel English and Chinese court judgments
